title: Twelve Points of Leverage: The Model Says Team Pillbert Fleeced The fumblers in the Diggs-for-Williams Swap
dek: Randy turned Javonte Williams into Stefon Diggs, and the title-odds calculator responded by more than doubling Alan's championship chances while trimming his own.
body: The deal itself is simple. Before Week 4, Randy's The fumblers sent running back Javonte Williams to Alan's Team Pillbert for wide receiver Stefon Diggs. Both players had spent all three weeks of the season on a roster, so this is a clean comparison: Williams arrives in Team Pillbert colors with 45.5 points, and Diggs lands with The fumblers carrying 38. That works out to roughly 15.2 points a week going to Alan and about 12.7 going to Randy, a gap of 7.5 points over three games.

Seven and a half points doesn't sound like a heist, but the title odds treat it like one. Team Pillbert jumped from 9% to 21%, a 12-point leap that more than doubles Philly's championship chances on a single transaction. The fumblers slipped from 16% to 14%. Add it up and the model sees a 14-point swing in Alan's favor, which is about as clear a verdict as a computer can deliver without banging a gavel.

Why such a big reaction? The likely answer is fit. A running back who has averaged 15 a week gives Team Pillbert a steadier floor in a backfield that, as recently as Week 3, watched De'Von Achane post 1.7 points on a 17.27 projection. Pair Williams with Jahmyr Gibbs and Alan suddenly has two backs who can carry a week, which matters a lot for a 2-1 team with playoff ambitions. Philly didn't just add points; he added insurance.

For Randy, the case for the deal is that a 3-0 team can afford to chase upside, and Diggs is a veteran receiver who could outscore those first three weeks the rest of the way. But the numbers say he gave up the more productive player, and the model docked him for it. For a manager whose trade activity is usually measured with a microscope, picking his one big swing to help the guy everyone loves rooting against is a choice the group chat will not let slide.

The verdict on paper: Team Pillbert wins this trade, and it isn't particularly close. Both new arrivals get an immediate test, with Williams joining Alan for the marquee showdown against Ramon's No Banner only HULK and Diggs debuting for The fumblers against Kaushal's winless Habibsters. If Diggs pops and Williams fizzles, Randy gets the last laugh. Until then, Alan has the receipts, and the receipts say 21%.

social.author: Odds Goblin
social.text: Team Pillbert title odds: 9% to 21%. The fumblers: 16% to 14%. That's a 14-point swing from one phone call. I've seen lopsided, but this one tilts.

social.author: Pillbert Nation
social.text: Gibbs AND Javonte. 45.5 points through three weeks walking in the door. HULK, we'll see you Sunday. Bring a backup plan.

social.author: Fumblers Faithful
social.text: Everybody relax. We're 3-0, Diggs has 38 points in three weeks, and the model has been wrong before. Habibsters, enjoy the welcome party.

social.author: BFL Insider Desk
social.text: Per sources, the per-week math is 15.2 for Williams vs 12.7 for Diggs. Per other sources, the league is already drafting the 'Randy funded the enemy' banner.
